diagnosis_hypotheses.note: Populace calculates benefits and recalibrates where CPS-ASEC carries survey-reported attributes; SPM level series therefore differ from ASEC-anchored series (CPSP, Census SPM). Observed at 2024: PE unforced 16.97% vs Census-published 13.4%; credit-take-up forcing accounts for ~0.2pp of the difference. Method registry links: populace PR#32 / census #9081 (SPM threshold treatment); channel decomposition (calculated-vs-reported benefits, recalibration, threshold treatment) lives in Max's pending policyengine-spm-decomposition project (not this lane); full record: results/us/SPM_NOTES.md. Descriptive classification per issue #9 (Max 8/2): not tied to a known issue in either system.

PE's higher measured level implies more children near the threshold, so scenario deltas scale up accordingly. CHANGE comparisons are the same_assumptions surface; directional consistency is the informative result.
newborn payment + birth-month proration omitted; refundable ODC non-refundable in PE (named, signed in scenario files)
CPSP 2024 brief computes credits via NBER TAXSIM on ASEC 2025; PE computes full tax law on populace ECPS.

early_head_start on the certified Build P artifact runs at engine-default 100% take-up (5.16M participants / $112.256B; take-up flag not stored) and its dollars flow inside household_net_income, so it is poverty-relevant and affects these level rows. Known-issue citation per the gating rule (calibration session verified scope 8/2); magnitude within the level difference not yet isolated. CHIP (also #593) is program-aggregate-only and does NOT affect these rows.
